subject: Beacon9b: telemetry blindspot & provisional version hold request
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Beacon9b: telemetry blindspot & provisional version hold request

Hi team,

Quick heads-up: we've started ingestion testing for BrightHealth's Beacon9b variant and the runtime telemetry is not emitting the KV cache hit/miss counters or per-request tokenization timing for sequences >1024. That gap means we can't validate the proposed batching/quantization profile for production traffic.

Why this matters: without those signals we can't confirm cost/latency projections and there is a risk of silent regressions during footprinted load tests. BrightHealth is asking for a canary in early October.

Ask: I'd like to request a provisional version pin (temporarily hold Beacon9b as a non-default serving variant) until we ship two items:
- a minimal compatibility telemetry patch (KV counters + tokenizer timing) deployed to staging, and
- a short sanity eval report that shows no >5% tail-latency regressions under 95th pct load for their prompt mix.

I've attached the compatibility template and initial failing traces. Can Laura/Aditya advise on implementation effort and Priyom on how disruptive a short pin would be for BrightHealth's go-live? If this looks heavy, we can scope a mitigation (partial telemetry + narrower canary).

Thanks,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Manager, Model Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon9b: telemetry blindspot & provisional version hold request

Thanks Mina — good catch. Quick notes after a first pass:

- Root cause: Beacon9b's tokenizer emits variable chunking for long sequences and our instrumentation hooks in the runtime assume fixed-tokenization events; KV-cache metrics are emitted but not correlated to the incremental tokenizer steps, so the dashboard shows zeros for some flows.
- Implementation plan: add a scoped hook to aggregate tokenization deltas and surface a per-request KV-hit/miss delta. I estimate ~2 dev-days to land in staging, plus 1 day of pipeline/metrics validation.
- Risk: minimal runtime overhead if we limit sampling to 10% of requests in staging.

Suggested next steps:
1) Approve provisional pin for Beacon9b in hosted staging and dedicated pools (non-default) until telemetry + sanity eval complete.
2) Run a focused canary (1% production tokens, isolated routing) after telemetry is live; collect 72h of signals.
3) If sanity eval shows no regressions, remove pin and proceed with standard rollout.

I can pick this up Friday and coordinate with infra to enable sampling. Aditya — can you confirm that sampling + aggregate hooks won't break any kernel selection paths? Priyom — what's the customer impact if we hold the variant for an extra 10 days?

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Sr. Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon9b: telemetry blindspot & provisional version hold request

On Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 10:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I can pick this up Friday and coordinate with infra to enable sampling. Aditya — can you confirm that sampling + aggregate hooks won't break any kernel selection paths?

Short answer: sampling hooks are safe. A few points:
- Kernel selection is triggered earlier based on model metadata and sequence-length distribution; the telemetry hook will run post-kernel-selection and only aggregates counters. It should not affect execution paths.
- We'll add the hook behind a feature flag to avoid any accidental exposure; we can roll the flag per-cluster.
- Perf overhead should be <1% when sampled at 10%.

I'll implement the flag + aggregate delta in the runtime repo and open a PR today. Laura — if you can schedule the validation window, Priyom and I will coordinate the canary config.

Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Nora Patel <nora@brighthealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightHealth Legal <legal@brighthealth.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beacon9b: telemetry blindspot & provisional version hold request

Hi Mina — thanks for flagging and thanks everyone for the quick analysis. A couple of notes from our side:

- We understand the need for the provisional hold, and we prefer the narrower canary (1% tokens then 72h signal) if that reduces timeline risk.
- Action items for BrightHealth: we can run our internal prompt mix through the staging endpoint and upload the first 24h traces to the Drive folder you linked. We will also need the sanity eval template so our ML team can match metrics.
- Legal: please note that if a provisional pin delays rollout beyond Oct 14th we will need a written exception path for SLA credits.

We'll start the 24h run tomorrow morning. Please confirm when the telemetry patch lands in staging and share the eval template (I've asked Priyom to coordinate).

Best,
Nora Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightHealth AI
